item.title: Why the Bond Market Remains Calm After the Blue Wave
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — For investors, the U.S. election was only one part of a much bigger equation. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Andrew Sheets discusses the balance of risks after the midterm results. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Andrew Sheets: Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I'm Andrew Sheets, Global Head of Fixed Income Research at Morgan Stanley. Today, what a blue wave means for fixed income. It's Friday, November 6th at 2pm in London. If the last decade has taught us anything, it's that financial professionals should approach political predictions and their market impact with a great deal of caution. With that caveat in mind, let's talk about Tuesday's U.S. midterms and what they might mean for fixed income. The word surprise has lost some meaning in investing over the years, but the U.S. election results qualify. Democrats won far more seats in both the House and the Senate than almost anyone expected. Key statewide races, such as Texas governor, also flipped unexpectedly. Democrats enjoyed the largest vote share of any party in almost 50 years. item.description: State Street · Street Signals — A surprisingly strong midterm election for US Democrats opens a myriad of questions for markets. From the scale of AI investment to the path of the Iran conflict, the changes in the makeup of the US government carry significant financial implications. Noel Dixon and Cayla Seder , senior macro strategists from our team in the US, join the podcast for a wrap-up and look ahead. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

item.title: Now You Can See Everything
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Eye on the Market — For the last couple of years, investors have wondered how voters would respond to the unorthodoxies of the second Trump Presidency. Now that midterms are over, You Can See Everything: it’s a rout, with the NYT projecting 53 Democratic Senators (plus 2 Independents that caucus with them) and 257 Democratic House members. In this Eye on the Market, we walk through the midterm results and economic/political factors around it, the implicit midterm referendum on AI and the latest AI-related market developments. Also, a section on You Can See Everything, Theranos, Elizabeth Holmes, David Boies, Tim Draper and a history of corporate fraud. Fraud is poison for markets, and investors should be equally unforgiving of people who commit it, condone it, conceal it or protect it. Watch the video
